proof.text: Work in the common universe $\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention], containing the fixed space, ring sheaf and a set $I$ of cardinality $\kappa$. For each open $U\subseteq Y$, put $\mathcal P_U=(W\mapsto\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal O_Y(W))^\#$ on the opens $W\subseteq U$, with coefficientwise restrictions. The free modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] give this actual module sheaf. Its canonical sections $e_i\in\mathcal P_U(U)$ have the following property: a family $m_i\in\mathcal N(U)$ defines the presheaf map $\sum a_i e_i\mapsto\sum a_i(m_i|_W)$, hence a unique sheaf map $\mathcal P_U\to\mathcal N$. Conversely any such map gives these sections, and uniqueness follows from the same sheafification universal property.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: If $\mathcal N$ on $U$ has a generating set $S_0\subseteq\mathcal N(U)$ of size at most $\kappa$, choose an injection $S_0\hookrightarrow I$ and pad the resulting family by zero. Step 1 gives $p:\mathcal P_U\to\mathcal N$. It is an epimorphism: if two module maps out of $\mathcal N$ agree after $p$, their difference kills every section in $S_0$. Its sectionwise kernel is a module subsheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and contains these generators. Since the sections generate $\mathcal N$ as a sheaf, this kernel is all of $\mathcal N$; the two maps agree. This uses precisely the sheaf-generation condition in the item, not surjectivity on sections.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: In the abelian category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], an epimorphism $p:P\to N$ is a cokernel of its kernel $k:K\to P$. Here is the argument from [def-sp-abelian]: write $p$ as a cokernel of some $f:H\to P$. Since $pf=0$, the kernel property factors $f$ through $k$. Every $g:P\to L$ killing $k$ therefore kills $f$, so factors uniquely through $p$. This is exactly the cokernel property for $k$. Thus $N$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{coker}(k)$ by the two cokernel universal properties, compatibly with the maps from $P$.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: For a fixed $U$, the module subsheaves $K\subseteq\mathcal P_U$ form a set $B_U$: they are a subset of $\prod_{W\subseteq U\ \mathrm{open}}\mathcal P(\mathcal P_U(W))$, cut out by closure under module operations, restrictions and the sheaf condition. For each such $K$ construct $Q_{U,K}$ as the module sheafification of $W\mapsto\mathcal P_U(W)/K(W)$; by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] this is the cokernel of $K\hookrightarrow\mathcal P_U$. Steps 2--3 show that every module on $U$ generated by at most $\kappa$ global sections is isomorphic to one of these $Q_{U,K}$. All products and power sets here are over sets in $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: Discard repeats in any generating open cover, choosing one generating family for each retained open. Possible covers are now subsets $C\subseteq\operatorname{Op}(Y)$ with union $Y$, so form a set. For each $C$ choose local indices $(K_U)_{U\in C}\in\prod_{U\in C}B_U$. For a fixed tuple the module isomorphisms $\phi_{UV}:Q_{U,K_U}|_{U\cap V}\to Q_{V,K_V}|_{U\cap V}$ form sets: a morphism is a family of functions on sections over the set of opens of $U\cap V$, subject to naturality and linearity [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; inverse pairs form a subset of two such function sets. Consequently the tuples $c=(C,(K_U),(\phi_{UV}))$ with $\phi_{UU}=1$ and $\phi_{VW}\phi_{UV}=\phi_{UW}$ on triple intersections form a set $E$.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the small site $\operatorname{Op}(Y)$, its terminal object $Y$, and each cover $C$ in a code $c\in E$. Fibre products are intersections; the stated identity and cocycle conditions are exactly its hypotheses. This gives a set sheaf $H_c$ and compatible local identifications with the underlying sheaves of $Q_{U,K_U}$. It becomes an $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaf: for sections $s,t$ on $W$, define $s+t$ by the unique gluing of the local sums on $W\cap U$; define $as$ from the local products by $a|_{W\cap U}$. These glue because each $\phi_{UV}$ is linear. Zero and negatives glue in the same way. The module identities and compatibility with restrictions hold after restriction to the cover, hence globally by uniqueness in the sheaf condition. Thus each local identification is linear. Make these choices over the set $E$ to obtain $(H_c)_{c\in E}$ in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 077M, lemma-set-of-iso-classes, proof; with Tag 077L, definition-kappa-generated.

proof.text: Let $T=\{c\in E\mid H_c\text{ is }\kappa\text{-generated in the sense of the item}\}$ and set $\mathcal M_c=H_c$ for $c\in T$. This is a small set-indexed family, and every member has the required property by construction. For any $\kappa$-generated $\mathcal M$, use a repeat-free generating cover $C$ and the local isomorphisms $a_U:\mathcal M|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{U,K_U}$ from steps 2--4. Set $\phi_{UV}=a_Va_U^{-1}$ on overlaps. Cancellation gives their cocycle, so these data give a code $c\in E$. The maps $a_U^{-1}$ composed with the local identifications of $H_c$ agree on overlaps, so [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] glues them to $H_c\to\mathcal M$, and glues their inverses to $\mathcal M\to H_c$. Their composites restrict to identities, hence are identities by uniqueness. Both maps are linear since this can be checked on each covering open. Thus $H_c\cong\mathcal M$, so $c\in T$. The empty cover when $Y=\varnothing$ gives the unique module sheaf there, and zero padding also handles an empty generating set. No quasi-coherence or topological finiteness assumption entered.

title: A set of representatives for locally bounded-generated module sheaves
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O_Y$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y$, and let $\kappa$ be an infinite cardinal. Call an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] $\kappa$-generated if there is an open cover $Y=\bigcup_{a\in A}V_a$ and, for every $a$, a set $S_a\subseteq\mathcal M(V_a)$ with $|S_a|\leq\kappa$ whose sections generate $\mathcal M|_{V_a}$ as a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{V_a}$-modules (equivalently, the germs of $S_a$ span every stalk over $V_a$). There are a small set $T$ and a family $(\mathcal M_t)_{t\in T}$ of $\kappa$-generated $\mathcal O_Y$-modules such that every $\kappa$-generated $\mathcal O_Y$-module is isomorphic to some $\mathcal M_t$. Neither quasi-coherence nor a finiteness or separation condition on $Y$ is required.
